chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who forgets the ghusl on Friday until he has prayed. He said: “If it is still within the time, then he must perform ghusl and repeat the prayer; and if the time has passed, then his prayer has been valid.”

So this report is to be understood as recommendation, and likewise what has been narrated concerning making up the ghusl of Friday on the following day, and performing it earlier on Thursday if missing it is feared—the proper understanding in it is recommendation, as we have explained.
(299) 31. What we have mentioned was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who leaves the ghusl of Friday out of forgetfulness or otherwise. He said: “If he was forgetful, then his prayer is complete; and if he was deliberate, then ghusl is more beloved to me, and if he has done so, then let him seek Allah’s forgiveness and not return to it.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: ritual bath, here specifically the Friday ghusl
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, the occasion of the recommended ghusl
key_terms.يُعِيدَ الصَّلَاةَ: repeat the prayer while still within its time

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the Friday ghusl and prays without it?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling on leaving the Friday ghusl and its effect on prayer. It indicates that the prayer remains valid, especially when omitted forgetfully, and that the reports commanding repetition are understood in the sense of recommendation rather than obligation.
